4_2.text: (1) This table uses the UN COFOG definition of Defence spending. Government commitments on NATO qualifying defence spending are evaluated using NATO definitions. The two are different and not comparable. NATO defence figures, for example, include pensions whereas in COFOG these are included in Social Protection. Details and figures on NATO defence expenditure can be found at the following link:

(2) Transactions in 2008-09 onwards have been affected by financial sector interventions. Increases in spending from 2020-21 have been affected by measures taken in response to Covid-19 and increases in the cost of living.

(3) Following implementation of ESA2010, Network Rail is now classified to Central Government. Consequently Total Managed Expenditure (TME) includes Network Rail spending in all years shown, however the actual expenditure of Network Rail only appears in the Department for Transport budget from 2015-16. The functional analysis shown includes Network Rail spending from 2015-16 and is therefore only included within ‘Total Expenditure on services’ from that year.

(4) From 2011-12 onwards, the transport function includes expenditure relating to the local government part of the TfL subsidiary, ‘Transport Trading Limited’ in order to align with Office for National Statistics treatment.

(5) From 2011-12 onwards the 'grant-equivalent element of student loans' is no longer part of the TES framework and has therefore been removed from the Education function. Therefore figures are not directly comparable between 2010-11 and 2011-12. A full explanation of this decision can be found in PESA 2016 Annex E.
(6) From 2010-11 onwards VAT-based payments are no longer deducted from EU transactions thus bringing these totals in-line with ESA10.
(7) This excludes the temporary effects of banks being classified to the public sector.

(2) GDP until 2025-26 is consistent with the latest figures from the Office for National Statistics (published 30 June 2026). GDP forecasts from 2026-27 onwards are from the Office for Budget Responsibility (Economic and fiscal outlook - 3 March 2026).

vintage_note: This history is from PESA Chapter 4, July 2026. The latest overview uses a separate workbook: Chapter 5 of the July 2026 spending statistics. Its source page was updated later. We keep a source record for each workbook. We do not mix their values. The sources round to different units. This history uses £0.1 billion. The overview uses £ million.
limitations: This source shows spending by area from 2003-04. Table 4.1 also gives TME for 1985-86 and 1995-96. Those two years cover TME only. The other earlier ten-year entries are not held here. Other official sources may hold older data. Each subcategory is part of its parent area. Do not add it again. The source rounds figures to one decimal place. This may cause small gaps in sums.
